PullRequest.Title: test: Align Node unit test timeouts with Electron
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

The Node test entry point creates its own Mocha instance, so the `--timeout=5000` passed to the outer Mocha CLI did not configure the tests it runs. They instead inherited Mocha's 2-second default.

- Match the Electron runner's defaults: 5 seconds locally and 30 seconds in Azure/GitHub CI.
- Forward explicit `--timeout` / `-t` options to the actual runner, including `0` to disable timeouts.
- Remove the npm script's fixed timeout so it does not override the CI default.
- Document the defaults and overrides. Explicit suite/test timeouts remain unchanged.

Motivated by the 2-second bootstrap timeout in [build 479318](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=479318). This fixes the shared runner configuration rather than adding individual timeout overrides.

## Validation

On Windows with the repository's downloaded Node binary:

- `& '.\.build\node\v24.20.0\win32-x64\node.exe' node_modules\mocha\bin\mocha.js test\unit\node\index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src\vs\base\test\common\async.test.ts` — **passed: 148 tests, 2 pending**.
- `& '.\.build\node\v24.20.0\win32-x64\node.exe' --check test\unit\node\index.js` — **passed**.
- `& '.\.build\node\v24.20.0\win32-x64\node.exe' node_modules\eslint\bin\eslint.js test\unit\node\index.js` — **passed**.
- `git --no-pager diff --check` — **passed**.
- A temporary subprocess harness exercising the npm script's arguments passed **8 scenarios**: local, Azure CI, and GitHub CI defaults; local and CI overrides; `-t`; disabled timeouts; and duration strings. Each also checked suite/test overrides. The temporary harness was removed.

No full compile or full unit suite was run; this change is limited to JavaScript test-runner configuration, the npm script, and documentation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local full or targeted Node unit-test run
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing npm/Mocha process bootstraps, discovers and imports modules, then runs tests serially. The changed timer matters only when a test exceeds its timeout; it adds no work to passing tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same process was launched with an ineffective outer-runner timeout option.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the test run; process count is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read runner configuration, create the crash directory, glob tests, and import selected modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bootstrap/discovery pass plus one import per selected module.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same filesystem work occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before test execution; placement and count are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing work scales with selected modules/tests. Extra failure latency scales with sequential hung tests: the local default changes from 2 to 5 seconds, while explicit overrides replace it.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One process; module loading and default Mocha test execution are serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh process per invocation; Node caches imports only within that process. The timeout has no cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: only the inner Mocha per-test timer changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of hung local tests is unknown; passing tests have unchanged runtime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the normal path has no extra work, and the bounded failure-delay tradeoff is intentional.

Scenarios.Scenario: CI full Node unit suite on Linux, macOS, and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each existing OS job starts one runner, performs unchanged filesystem discovery/imports, and executes tests serially. The 30-second timer affects only over-limit tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch `npm run test-node` in each enabled OS job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same jobs launched one runner whose inner Mocha used its 2-second default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Contains the suite critical path; launch count is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read configuration, create the crash directory, discover tests, and import modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery pass and one import per selected module in each job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes execution but is unchanged by the timeout option.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing cost scales with suite size. Failure latency can scale with sequential hung tests at 30 seconds each, bounded by the workflow job timeout; passing tests are unaffected.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: OS jobs may run independently, but each job has one serial Mocha run. Existing workflow limits cap jobs at 15 or 30 minutes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Independent fresh CI processes/workspaces; no timeout cache or changed coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call sites, serial runner flow, and job caps are established in repository files.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of genuinely hung tests is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: no normal-path CPU, I/O, process, or concurrency increase; longer failure detection is intentional and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed every changed hunk and traced local and CI runner paths. Only the inner Mocha timeout changes; existing process, filesystem, serial execution, and cache behavior remain unchanged. No reportable performance regression or qualifying regression-fix record was found.
